clue.text: Part in playwright's "White Feather" for this

indicators.note: in tells us the actor's part is placed inside the dramatist's name with its possessive

parts.note: Noel Coward was an English playwright; with the possessive his name gives COWARDS
an actor's part is the lines he or she speaks

explanation.surface: A clue promising a role in a play called White Feather, written by some dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' does the placing, and the possessive's S stays in the answer. Noel Coward was an English playwright; 'Part' is an actor's role, not a portion.
explanation.definitionFit: A white feather has long been handed to men as a symbol of supposed timidity and lack of courage in war.

clue.text: Excellent, I say

definitions.meaning: an old exclamation of delight, like 'Splendid!'

explanation.walkthrough: As an exclamation the word is old-fashioned British slang for 'Splendid!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital means first-rate, and as a dated British exclamation it expresses approval, like 'jolly good'.

clue.text: Garcon! I am wanting a drink

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letter I is taken out

parts.note: garcon is French for waiter, the word used to call one
I is taken as written

explanation.surface: A diner calls the waiter and says they would like something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I am wanting' reads as 'I would like', but 'wanting' means lacking: WAITER without I.
explanation.definitionFit: Water is the most basic beverage, something you would order to sip.

clue.text: Replacement ticket for artist under control

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
under control is held in check

explanation.surface: A substitute pass for a painter who is kept on a tight rein.
explanation.definitionFit: A rain check is a ticket for a later game given when a match is rained off.

clue.text: Put down face up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for face is read from the bottom

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock or watch

explanation.surface: An instruction to lay something with its front showing.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid is the past form of lay, so put down as in placed on a surface.

clue.text: No Poles follow non-U rats

parts.note: taken as written
N and S are the north and south poles

indicators.note: non-U, read literally, means without U, so that letter is removed

parts.note: to follow is to ensue

explanation.surface: A snobbish remark that Polish people are not imitating lower-class rodents.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is Nancy Mitford's label for language not used by the upper class; here it means 'without U', taking U out of ENSUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rats! is an exclamation dismissing something as rubbish or absurd.

clue.text: Island's climbing antelope

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word reads upwards

parts.note: Elba is an island, Napoleon's place of exile; with the 's it gives ELBAS

explanation.surface: An antelope scrambling up an island's slopes.
explanation.definitionFit: The sable antelope is a large African antelope with long curved horns.

clue.text: Imprisoning one such as Owen Glendower, Henry made a bloomer

indicators.note: imprisoning means the name for Henry holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: Hal is the familiar name for Prince Henry in Shakespeare's Henry IV
Owen Glendower was a Welsh rebel against Henry IV

explanation.surface: King Henry jails the Welsh rebel and makes a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bloomer' looks like a blunder but is a flower. Glendower leads the rebels in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 1, in which Prince Hal fights them.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer here is literally a plant that flowers; the harebell is a blue wild flower.

clue.text: Saint surrounded by a sort of light in part of church

indicators.note: surrounded by means the abbreviation for saint is encircled by the other piece

parts.note: a Very light is a coloured signal flare fired from a pistol

explanation.surface: A halo around a saint inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: A Very light is a signal flare named after its inventor; 'surrounded by' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The vestry is the room in a church where robes and sacred vessels are kept.

clue.text: Noble pair I can't corrupt

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or perverted, so the letters of pair I can't are reworked

explanation.surface: An aristocratic pair whom someone cannot bribe.
explanation.definitionFit: A patrician was a member of the hereditary aristocracy of ancient Rome, hence any aristocrat.

clue.text: Live, pierced by boy's sword

indicators.note: pierced by means the word for live has something driven into its middle

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist
a boy is a lad

explanation.surface: A youth's weapon stabs through something living.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade is a literary term for a sword, from the cutting part of the weapon.

clue.text: Bellman thus speaks truly

parts.note: In Lewis Carroll's The Hunting of the Snark the Bellman says that what he tells you three times is true, so repeating a statement that many times is how he speaks truly

explanation.surface: A town crier delivering his announcements honestly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bellman is the captain in Carroll's nonsense poem The Hunting of the Snark, whose rule is 'What I tell you three times is true.'
explanation.definitionFit: The Bellman's rule is that a statement repeated three times is true, so he speaks truly by saying things that many times.

clue.text: Passionate, virile chaps during prohibition mostly

indicators.note: during means the virile chaps come within the word for prohibition
mostly means the word for prohibition loses its last letter

parts.note: a veto is a prohibition
virile chaps are he-men

explanation.surface: Strongly felt feelings among macho men in the era of Prohibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims the ban word to VET, and 'during' signals the container; 'prohibition' suggests the US era but just means a ban.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement means showing strong feeling, so a passionate argument is a forceful one.

clue.text: In hospital I sterilized everything for surgeon

indicators.note: In tells us the answer sits within the words hospital I sterilized

explanation.surface: A nurse boasting of having sterilised all the instruments for the surgeon in the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals the run of letters across 'hospital I sterilized'. Joseph Lister pioneered antiseptic surgery, which makes the sterilising surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Lister was the Victorian surgeon who pioneered antiseptic operating methods.

clue.text: Bill's turned up an article that's very critical

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the word for bill reads upwards

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill; with the 's it gives ACS
an article is an object, a thing

explanation.surface: Someone's invoice comes back, carrying a review that pulls no punches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses ACS (account's) to SCA. 'article' looks like a newspaper piece or grammatical word, but it means a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Scathing describes harsh, severe criticism, such as a withering review.

clue.text: Disturbing rest, play a musical instrument

indicators.note: Disturbing means throwing into disorder, so the letters of rest and play are reworked

explanation.surface: An instruction to break the quiet by playing some instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A psaltery is an ancient stringed instrument plucked with the fingers, a kind of zither.

clue.text: Hun endlessly invaded chaotic Italian republic

indicators.note: invaded means the shortened Hun goes inside the other letters
chaotic means disordered, so the letters of Italian are reworked
endlessly means the last letter of Hun is taken off

explanation.surface: A Hun tribesman overrunning a disorderly Italian state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chaotic' makes LITANIA, 'endlessly' trims the barbarian, and 'invaded' signals the container. 'Hun' looks like the attacker of the surface, which it is, cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithuania is a Baltic state, a republic in northern Europe.

clue.text: Search, and one turned up, no doubt

parts.note: a search is a quest
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the word no reads upwards

explanation.surface: A hunt in which someone appeared, undoubtedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no doubt' reads as one phrase, but 'no' is reversed and 'doubt' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To call something into question is to doubt it, so the two words are synonyms here.

clue.text: Withdaw, getting left in the dark

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for left goes within the phrase meaning withdraw

parts.note: to withdraw from a deal is to back out

explanation.surface: Someone pulls out of a scheme and is kept uninformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the dark' looks like the idiom for uninformed, but 'in' places L inside BACK OUT and 'the dark' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackout is a period of total darkness when lights are put out, as in a power cut or wartime.

clue.text: Spirit produced by investing. money overseas

indicators.note: investing means clothing, so the word by wraps around the money

parts.note: the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: A drink paid for by putting cash into foreign ventures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing' looks financial but means clothing or enclosing; the rand is South Africa's currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a spirit distilled from wine.

clue.text: Lacking emotion, one's told, is wrong

indicators.note: wrong means out of order, so the letters of the pieces are reworked

parts.note: one is I, and with the 's it gives IS

explanation.surface: Someone is informed that showing no feelings is a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges IS (one's, I plus 's) with TOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolid describes a calm, impassive person who shows little feeling.

clue.text: Surgeon's assistant works in the theatre

definitions.meaning: one who dresses wounds in hospital
one who helps actors into their costumes

explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' suggests an operating theatre after 'Surgeon', but the second sense is the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital orderly who bandages wounds, and a backstage helper who looks after an actor's costumes, share this title.

clue.text: Using an optical device round the house, saw a gnome

parts.note: an gives the letter A

indicators.note: round means the optical device is placed around the abbreviation for house

parts.note: a prism is an optical device that splits light

explanation.surface: Someone with binoculars or a telescope near home spots a garden gnome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gnome' looks like a garden ornament, but it is an old word for a pithy saying. 'round' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnome in this sense is a short maxim, like a proverb or saying that states a general truth.

clue.text: Send race official up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for the official reads upwards

parts.note: a timer records the times in a race

explanation.surface: An instruction to dispatch a racing official upward.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit is to send money or refer a matter to another body.

clue.text: What juggernauts do to twig

definitions.meaning: heavy lorries make a deep rolling noise as they pass
to twig is to realise or see through something

explanation.walkthrough: A juggernaut is the British name for a very large lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Big lorries make a low rolling sound as they pass, and to see through a trick or plot is also to find it out.

clue.text: Assassin in theatre stall

definitions.meaning: John Wilkes ... shot Abraham Lincoln at Ford's Theatre in Washington
a small enclosed stand or kiosk

explanation.definitionFit: John Wilkes Booth killed President Lincoln at Ford's Theatre, and a small market stand or kiosk has the same name.

clue.text: With "excited eagerness in abundance, almost

indicators.note: almost means the phrase for in abundance loses its last letter

parts.note: a gogo, from French, means in plenty

explanation.surface: Keen enthusiasm present in great quantity, nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a gogo' is an informal phrase for in abundance (as in 'whisky a gogo'); 'almost' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means eagerly expectant, keen to hear or see something.

clue.text: Dug around for material

indicators.note: around means the word for dug is turned to read the other way

parts.note: dug in the sense of excavated is mined

explanation.surface: Someone digs about looking for cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a hard-wearing twilled cotton fabric used for jeans.

clue.text: Using one I made a move that's cleverly contrived

indicators.note: made a move means the letters shift position, so using one I is reworked

explanation.surface: A chess player who makes a move with just one piece that is cunningly planned.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingenious describes a device or plan that is original and well thought out.

clue.text: Office worker's gone back, wearing tie in front of lady

indicators.note: wearing means the tie is put on around the other piece

parts.note: a strap ties something down, so it is a tie

indicators.note: back means the word gone is read the other way round

parts.note: her refers to a lady

explanation.surface: A clerk has left, sporting a necktie and walking ahead of a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' makes ENOG, 'wearing' signals the container, and 'in front of' orders the final charade; 'Office worker's' hides 'has' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stenographer takes dictation in shorthand, a traditional clerical job.
